reproFailure: At base, before the fix: 15 of 23 cases failed. Gap 1: `AssertionError: expected +0 to be 2` from countReportResults on a load-failure report, and `expected 3 to be +0` from `history record` exiting 3 on it. Gap 2 was proven by planting: with keyedName removed, 3 cases fail, including `gives one file the same test_name from two checkouts`.
premiseEvidence: Reports generated by real Playwright 1.64.1 with the JSON reporter, 15 scenarios. Gap 1 is real, but the issue misdescribes its effect for the load-failure case: a spec that fails to load aborts the whole run, `suites` is empty, and `record` abstained (exit 3, nothing stored). `Fewer failures than happened` is the throwing-globalTeardown shape: tests intact, `failed: 0` stored, Playwright exit 1.
closingKeywordWhy: Both gaps are fixed. Gap 1: one failed row per real top-level error, and those errors count toward the denominator. Gap 2: the synthetic name follows test_file to the repo-relative key.
assumptions: Recorded for the human: making the synthetic name repo-relative changes test_name, and flake and timeline queries key on it. Existing rows under the old absolute name stop joining and age out of the window. No migration, by instruction.

`record` on a Playwright load-failure report now exits 0 and stores a failed run, where it used to abstain with exit 3. That is the fix: the count is the gate, so a reader-only change would never have been reached through the CLI.

`No tests found` and `Testing stopped early after N maximum allowed failures` are not rows. The first is an empty denominator (it stays an abstention) or the echo of a load error; the second restates test failures already counted. Matched on text, only for errors with no location, so a reworded notice shows up as a failed row rather than dropping a real failure.

An error with no location (webServer failed, globalTimeout) is named `(run failed outside any test)` with an empty test_file, counted as unjoinable, as JUnit rows with no file already are. The message is not part of the name, because messages embed absolute paths and would recreate gap 2.

One row per error, literally: a helper imported by two specs yields two rows at the same file, the second named with a ` #2` suffix. Distinct names because flake counters add one per row, so a shared name would count one history twice in one run.
An error thrown outside the repo's tree (or with no git repo) keeps the name as written and is counted in unjoinableTestFiles, the same rule test_file already follows.

readReplayStatus now joins a stored repo-relative synthetic name to the path the reader wrote. Without this, the rename would have made `canary rewind` report a reproduced load failure as `report does not hold that test`.
New module ts/src/history/formats/playwright-errors.ts rather than growing playwright-report.ts past the 300-line per-file limit (it would have reached 314; it is 237 now).
Remote store: no change; rows have the existing TestResultInput shape.

fixes.finding: canary rewind gave false `reproduced` for a failure outside any test: an unanchored suffix match let another file answer (M1), and a clean attempt had no row, so it was dropped and the repeat count could not say intermittent (M2).
assumptions: F6=A as answered: the notice regex anchor, malformed errors entries, the false no-file reason and the CHANGELOG entry ship in this push.
A malformed `errors` entry (non-string message or location.file) is ignored, so a report holding only such entries abstains as the base did.
Playwright replays of a synthetic target drop `--grep`: real Playwright 1.64.1 answers a grep on the synthetic title with empty `suites`, so a clean load could never be told from an unselected file.
A numbered target (` #2`) whose file ran without that row counts as passed: that error did not recur.
A row stored under the old absolute name is matched through its repo-relative test_file, so a failing attempt is not misread as passed.
An attempt that cannot show the file ran is not counted, as for any other test. So 1 failure plus 4 uncounted attempts still reads `reproduced`, tracked in #1584.
